Schedule 2-hour pilot kickoff w/ infra team week of Jan 11
action_items: Maya Patel - send cost-mapping template and sample queries - 2027-01-06
Carlos Mendes - run quick lab to reproduce BlueCrest 1k qps profile and share perf numbers - 2027-01-10

summary: Walkthrough of Redwood Console features for translating traffic/route activity into billable cost buckets. Focus on per-route dashboards, tagging, and how to map model variants and KV cache/batching settings to cost attribution. Customer is evaluating hosted vs dedicated for a clinical inference workflow; major concerns: data residency, audit logs, predictable monthly spend.
topics: KV cache and batching effect on unit cost
transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date/Time: 2027-01-03 16:00 UTC
- Duration: ~52m
- Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Carlos (Redwood SE), Priya (Redwood CSM), Jordan (BlueCrest), Aisha (BlueCrest), Tom (BlueCrest finance), Sofia (BlueCrest security)

Summary note: demo focused on how console turns traffic (routes) into billing line-items, and how to surface anomalies. Links shared: https://redwood.ai/decks/traffic-to-bill, spreadsheet: https://redwood.ai/samples/bc-cost-template

[00:00] Maya: hey everyone thanks for joining, can you all hear me okay?
[00:05] Jordan: yeah good, loud and clear, thanks Maya.
[00:12] Maya: cool quick agenda: we'll show the Console route view, how we map requests to cost buckets, then dig into a per-route dashboard and show how batching and prefix cache change the numbers. carlos will demo the lab and then we'll cover security questions at the end. sound good?
[00:25] Aisha: yep that's perfect, especially the batching part we need that for throughput planning.
[00:30] Carlos: hi all, I'll jump in around the 12 minute mark with the sandbox run but quick clarifying q: are you evaluating hosted or dedicated for the initial pilot?
[00:38] Tom: finance is leaning hosted to avoid capex, but they want predictable monthly caps.
[00:44] Jordan: from ML ops side we're leaning dedicated later for low variance but pilot is hosted.
[00:50] Maya: great that matches the typical path. ok i'll share my screen — console home —

[01:05] Maya: first up the Routes index: you can see each route rows include traffic (rps), model variant, avg latency, tokens per request, and a cost per 1k requests projection. so for bluecrest we would provide a per-route mapping like this — you can rename routes, attach tags.
[01:25] Aisha: can you map k8s ingress paths to routes? our traffic uses path-based routing and a proxy that strips headers.
[01:32] Carlos: yes we do path and header mapping; we also have an extraction step in our SDK so we can attribute to "clinical-ocr" or "triage-clarify" route names even if front proxy mutates them. sometimes the transcription will show old header names (we call that extraction mismatch).
[01:48] Jordan: ok, good — and how do you deal with multi-tenant requests where one call fans out to multiple models?
[01:55] Maya: two ways — one is route composition: we show primary route and also sub-calls in the waterfall, each with their own token counts; the other is cost-join where you can split cost by rule (percentage or tokens). we can demo a sample where the NLP step calls a reranker and an embedding service.
[02:14] Tom: finance question — how deterministic are the per-route cost numbers month-over-month? last month we had a spike that doubled token usage due to a bad prompt.
[02:23] Priya: we see that a lot — Console has anomaly alerts and a cost-forecast projection that accounts for moving averages and an outlier detection. you can set a hard cap and we support automated fallback to lower-cost model variants when threshold hit.
[02:40] Sofia: security: do you retain request bodies in the audit log and for how long? we need 7 years for some clinical audit trails.
[02:49] Carlos: by default we store metadata and hashed payloads; for Private/Dedicated you control retention and can ship logs to your SIEM. for hosted we have SOC2 controls and longer retention is part of an enterprise add-on. we'll share the security packet.
[03:05] Maya: ok demo time — carlos take it away with the sandbox that mimics 1k rps with triage and ocr routes.

[03:15] Carlos: launching sandbox now — i'm running a synthetic workload: 60% triage-clarify route, 30% clinical-ocr, 10% admin-chat. starting baseline run with no batching and no prefix cache.
[03:35] Carlos: results coming in — avg latency 210ms per request, tokens/request ~420, cost projection $5.80 per 1k req on xlarge model.
[03:50] Aisha: that cost seems high compared to our estimates — can you break out tokenization vs model compute?
[03:58] Carlos: sure, in the per-route panel we split token cost and compute cost. tokens are ~60% of line-item here because of long clinical notes.
[04:10] Maya: note that those numbers don't include KV cache savings or batching — we'll run with those next.
[04:20] Carlos: now enabling continuous batching at 50ms window and turning on prefix/KV cache for triage-clarify route. re-run.
[04:35] Carlos: new numbers: avg latency bump to 230ms for some requests due to batch wait but 1k-req cost drops to $3.25 — huge per-token savings because of cache hits and amortized attention.
[04:50] Jordan: that's interesting — slight latency tradeoff, big cost upside. our SLA target for triage is 200ms P90 though — any way to get both?
[04:59] Carlos: yes a couple options: smaller batch windows, dynamic batching only on low priority routes, or serve hot-path with a pinned lower-latency variant (quantized) in Dedicated to meet SLO. Console can show per-route latency SLO breaches and suggest policy changes via Optimize recommendations.
[05:20] Maya: showing the Optimize tab — here we provide recommendations: suggest quantized 8-bit variant for high-volume non-critical routes, suggest batch window 30ms for triage, and advise persistent KV cache with 95% hit target. you can accept suggestions or tune.
[05:40] Tom: if we accept recommendations, is the cost delta guaranteed? finance wants to model best and worst case.
[05:46] Priya: recommendations include conservative + optimistic estimates; we also produce a simulated month projection based on current traffic and the accepted config. not a SLA for cost but helps planning.
[05:58] Aisha: how are network egress costs treated? our data residency means we might deploy in eu-west-2 and have internal egress rules.
[06:06] Carlos: Console lets you set region mapping per route and the cost calc includes region-specific infra unit costs. for private deployments you have full control and the chart will reflect your on-prem marginal cost if you input that.
[06:20] Maya: quick detour on tagging: you can attach multi-level tags (team, product, environment). we map those to billing groups so finance can do chargebacks.
[06:32] Tom: will the chargeback show raw token counts per team? we need that in our internal GL.
[06:37] Maya: yes exportable CSV per billing period with token counts, compute hrs, and allocated spend by tag.
[06:45] Jordan: can you show an example of a cost-surge alert going off?
[06:50] Carlos: clicking into Alerts — here's a simulated surge for clinical-ocr — console flagged a >2x token rate and opened an incident. it suggests rollback to a lighter model or apply a rate limit.
[07:05] Sofia: what about PII redaction in logs? can we mask PHI in logs before retention?
[07:12] Carlos: we support field-level redaction in the SDK and can hash or redact request text in the audit trail. for Private installs customers can run their own redaction pipeline before logs land in Redwood.
[07:25] Maya: okay we're about 20 minutes in — opening Q/A, feel free to throw hypothetical scenarios.
[07:33] Jordan: scenario: we have a multi-step NLP pipeline - OCR -> extraction -> clinical tagging -> reranker. how does console attribute cost if one front-end route triggers all?
[07:44] Carlos: we show a waterfall timeline per request that lists subcalls with their own token counts; you can choose attribution rules: attribute to first caller, split by token, or custom rule. we'll include the waterfall CSV when we send the template.
[08:00] Tom: for procurement: contract length impacts unit price — any flexibility on burst capacity?
[08:08] Maya: yes Dedicated includes burst credits; hosted has burst pools subject to quota. for pricing we can model a committed monthly baseline and then per-token overage. we'll send sample pricing scenarios.
[08:20] Aisha: are there any gotchas with our proxy terminating TLS and adding headers?
[08:25] Carlos: proxy behavior is common; we offer header normalization and an SDK hook. occasionally the transcription will mislabel headers (in the export) so we recommend a short handoff test.
[08:40] Maya: demoing the per-route dashboard now — top chart is request rate, second is cost per minute, third is token distribution, bottom is downstream calls. you can filter by tag and by date range.
[08:58] Carlos: notice the heatmap for token size by hour — in your case we expect morning batch jobs to spike tokens. you can schedule autoscale policies per route.
[09:12] Jordan: any way to tie this back to product metrics — i.e., conversions per dollar spent?
[09:18] Maya: yes we have a metrics join where you can upload external KPIs or connect to your BI; then Console surfaces cost per conversion or cost per successful classification.
[09:30] Tom: finance wants a sample month model with worst-case surge and typical.
[09:36] Maya: noted — action: we'll fill out the sample sheet and send a worst/typical projection.
[09:42] Priya: also adding notes about how batching policies were tuned in the demo.
[09:48] Aisha: can we restrict which routes can call which model variants? we want to avoid accidental high-cost model calls from admin tools.
[09:56] Carlos: yes policy controls at route level allow whitelist of model families and a fallback variant. you can set guardrails in the routing policy.
[10:08] Sofia: last security question: do you do key wrapping with our HSM or is it Redwood-managed?
[10:14] Carlos: for Private and Dedicated we support customer-managed KMS/HSM; for hosted we manage keys but offer envelope encryption and dedicated key options for enterprise.
[10:25] Maya: ok wrapping up — recap and next steps.
[10:29] Maya: next steps: we'll send the cost-mapping spreadsheet, security packet, and propose pilot kickoff for Jan 11. carlos will run a lab with the 1k rps profile and share perf numbers. aisha will share tagging schema.
[10:45] Jordan: sounds good, thanks all.
[10:48] Tom: appreciate the clarity on chargeback exports.
[10:52] Maya: great meeting — we'll follow up by email with attachments. thanks everyone.

Post-meeting notes:
- Shared links: deck and spreadsheet (see header).
- Noted risk: BlueCrest's P90 latency SLO for triage is tight; may require dedicated pinned variant or shorter batch windows.
- Billing model to propose: committed baseline + overage with per-route reporting and chargeback CSV to finance.

(Transcript shows occasional speaker label mismatches and a few ASR mis-transcriptions — e.g. "KV cache" transcribed as "K V cash" in export.)
